review_metadata.facet_definition: Own-Policy-Adherence: Algorithm. Cryptographic primitives correctly chosen, HLC algorithm correct (Demirbas + Kulkarni 2014), shuffle sharding math correct, SLO composition Markov chain correct, Cedar evaluation correctness.
review_metadata.reviewer_lens: A7 — algorithm-level technical correctness; mathematical, cryptographic, and protocol specification scrutiny

verdict_summary: The keystone bundle exhibits strong overall algorithmic literacy and grounds its choices in canonical sources (Demirbas+Kulkarni HLC, MacCárthaigh shuffle sharding, NIST FIPS 203/204, RFC 9420 MLS, IEEE 1588 PTP, Brooker constant work, Weiss/Furr static stability). All core primitives are correctly selected and well-cited. However, the review identifies (1) a precision defect in the SLO Markov composition formulation in ADR-0280, (2) a subtle but real correctness gap in the HLC pseudocode initial-state handling and the 16-bit logical counter overflow case in ADR-0252, (3) an arithmetic verification miss on the shuffle-sharding 'simultaneous cell failures' example in ADR-0248, (4) ambiguity in ADR-0253's claim that AES-128 vs AES-256 against Grover gives equivalent post-quantum strength when AES-128-GCM is the default, and (5) several specification-completeness gaps around ML-KEM-768 KDF binding and Ed25519 nonce-misuse boundaries. Findings are addressable as F-class fixes prior to BLOCKER promotion; no algorithmic decision needs to be reversed.

evidence.notes: Ed25519 chosen for deterministic signatures, side-channel resistance, FIPS-186-5 acceptance (Feb 2023). All usage sites align with RFC 8032. Rationale and rotation cadences are appropriate (quarterly for region webhook keys; per-epoch for MLS group leaves).
X25519 is the canonical modern ECDH curve; patent-free; matches RFC 7748 + RFC 9180 HPKE composition. Hybrid composition with ML-KEM-768 follows draft-ietf-tls-hybrid-design convention.
AES-128-GCM is correct for AEAD; nonce derivation per RFC 9420 §9 is structurally safe (key+counter). Finding A7-F4 below questions the post-quantum security argument.

usage_sites: MLS standard §3.4 AEAD fallback for non-AES-NI
evidence.notes: Correct fallback for devices without AES-NI; matches Mozilla 'modern' TLS profile.
ML-KEM-768 = NIST level III is the correct PQ KEM target. Hybrid concatenation pattern (HKDF over both shared secrets) is sound. See finding A7-F5 on KDF binding specification.
ML-DSA-65 = NIST level III matches ML-KEM-768 strength. Dual-sign pattern is acceptable.
Domain-separated via labels per RFC 9420 §8 — correctly described.
SHA-256 is appropriate; HMAC-style construction in idempotency-key hash is correct.
Stripe-style HMAC + modern Ed25519 dual-sign migration is the right pattern.
M-of-N Shamir is the canonical root-key custody pattern; aligned with HashiCorp Vault / OpenBao practice.
TreeKEM as O(log N) group key agreement is correctly described; epoch advancement semantics correctly stated; FS+PCS properties correctly attributed.
TLS 1.0/1.1/1.2 disabled is the correct posture; cipher-suite list matches Mozilla 'modern'.

crypto_primitive_correctness.summary: All cryptographic primitives are correctly chosen and align with canonical sources. The post-quantum migration plan (X25519+ML-KEM-768 hybrid; Ed25519+ML-DSA-65 dual-sign) follows the IETF hybrid pattern and NIST FIPS 203/204. Findings are specification-completeness gaps, not primitive-selection errors.

shuffle_sharding.source_referenced: Colm MacCárthaigh, AWS Architecture Blog 2014-08-19 'Shuffle Sharding: Massive and Magical Fault Isolation'
shuffle_sharding.core_formula: P(full overlap between tenants A and B) = 1 / C(C, S)

checks.claim: On a single cell failure: 8% of tenants experience degradation in 1 of their 8 cells, capacity reduced by 12.5%
checks.verification: Expected fraction of tenants present in any given cell = S/C = 8/100 = 8%. Correct.

checks.claim: On two simultaneous cell failures: expected 8/100 × 7/99 ≈ 0.566% of tenants have BOTH failed cells in shard
checks.verification: P(both of two specific failed cells in a tenant's shard) = C(98,6)/C(100,8) = (8*7)/(100*99) = 56/9900 ≈ 0.5657%. Approximation 8/100 × 7/99 ≈ 0.005657 ≈ 0.566% — VERIFIED.

checks.claim: On three simultaneous cell failures: ~0.058% of tenants have all three failed in shard
checks.verification: P(all three specific failed cells in tenant's 8-shard) = (8*7*6)/(100*99*98) = 336/970200 ≈ 3.463e-4 ≈ 0.0346%. The ADR claims 0.058%. ARITHMETIC DEFECT: 0.058% does not match the binomial computation. The correct value is ~0.0346% (≈ 5.8x smaller than the next-cell-failure scaling would naively suggest if the author chained 0.566% × 6/98 ≈ 0.0346%; the printed 0.058% appears to be a transcription error).
checks.recommended_fix: Replace '~0.058%' with '~0.035%' in ADR-0248 §D-7. The 37.5% bounded-capacity-loss conclusion is unaffected; only the probability is wrong.

checks.claim: S=8 shard width with home_cell + dr_cell + 6 read replicas
checks.verification: Architecture matches MacCárthaigh's framing; bounded blast radius properties preserved.

shuffle_sharding.summary: Shuffle sharding math is correctly grounded in MacCárthaigh 2014; combinatorics are correct except for a transcription error in the 3-cell-failure probability (cited 0.058% should be ~0.035%). Material conclusions (no full tenant outage; bounded capacity loss) are unaffected.

checks.issue: Markov chain claim vs actual formulation
checks.analysis: ADR-0280 describes the SLO composition as 'deterministic Markov-chain bound' and as 'Markov-chain multiplication'. The formula given (∏ᵢ (1 - wᵢ × (1 - SLO_Dᵢ))) is NOT a Markov chain — it is a weighted independence-of-failures product approximation. A true Markov-chain composition would model state-transition probabilities between availability states. The formula is closer to a 'weighted product-form availability bound under failure-independence assumption with linear dependency weighting'. The naming 'Markov chain' is technically inaccurate.
checks.recommended_fix: Either (a) rename 'Markov-chain composition' to 'weighted independence-product composition' or 'dependency-weighted availability product', OR (b) actually model the SLO composition as a discrete Markov chain over (UP, DEGRADED, DOWN) states per substrate with transition probabilities derived from each substrate's MTTF/MTTR. Option (a) is cheaper and is recommended for the keystone landing; option (b) is a follow-up ADR worth filing.

checks.analysis: The formula ∏ᵢ (1 - wᵢ × (1 - SLO_Dᵢ)) assumes substrate failures are INDEPENDENT. In practice, cell-correlated failures (one cell going down takes multiple substrate replicas hosted in that cell) violate independence. The ADR does not state this assumption.
checks.recommended_fix: Add a paragraph in ADR-0280 §D-6 explicitly noting: 'This formula assumes substrate failures are independent. For cell-correlated failure modes (multiple substrates in the same cell), the bound is loose; chaos-engineering drills per §D-8 validate that empirical availability stays within the bound.'

Re-run the product computation in ADR-0280 §D-6 with at least 7 significant digits per term and update the result. The qualitative point (~99.85% upper bound) is unchanged; the precise digit should be corrected for engineer trust.

checks.issue: Dependency-weight semantics — what does 'weight 0.7' mean exactly?
checks.analysis: The formula treats weight as a linear scaler on the dependency's unavailability contribution. But the cascade_rule enum {FULL, DEGRADED, BROWNOUT, INDEPENDENT} carries semantic meaning that is partially redundant with weight (FULL≈1.0; DEGRADED≈0.5; BROWNOUT≈0.3). The ADR does not explicitly tie the cascade_rule to the dependency_weight; readers must infer. Risk: future authors set incompatible (rule, weight) pairs (e.g., FULL + 0.3).
checks.recommended_fix: In ADR-0280 §D-1, add a validator constraint that dependency_weight values are bounded by the cascade_rule: FULL ⇒ weight==1.0; DEGRADED ⇒ 0.5≤weight<1.0; BROWNOUT ⇒ 0<weight<0.5; INDEPENDENT ⇒ weight==0. Add a CI check 'oya-check-substrate-cascade-rule-weight-coherence'.

slo_markov_composition.summary: The SLO composition formulation is approximately correct in spirit but mis-named ('Markov' is incorrect terminology for an independence-product), has unstated independence assumption, and the worked-example arithmetic is slightly off. None of these affect the doctrine's safety; they are precision defects worth addressing before BLOCKER promotion.

hlc_algorithm.source_referenced: Demirbas, M. & Kulkarni, S. 'Logical Physical Clocks and Consistent Snapshot Isolation' OPODIS 2014, arXiv:1407.5208

pseudocode_review.structure: Two cases: local event (M is None) and message receipt (M is not None)

local_event_case.claim: if pt > N.last_pt: pt' = pt, l' = 0; else: pt' = N.last_pt, l' = N.last_l + 1

message_receipt_case.claim: Computes pt_max as max of (N.last_pt, M.hlc.pt, monotonic_wall_clock_now_ms()); then branches on which is maximum
message_receipt_case.verification: The structure matches the canonical algorithm. The three-way max + per-case logical-counter rule is the published form.

issues_identified.analysis: The pseudocode references N.last_pt and N.last_l but does not specify their initial values when a node starts cold. Per the Demirbas-Kulkarni paper, the conventional initialization is N.last_pt = 0, N.last_l = 0, but the ADR does not state this. An uninitialized HLC state could produce non-monotonic outputs in production code.
issues_identified.recommended_fix: In ADR-0252 §D-1, add: 'Initial state: N.last_pt = 0, N.last_l = 0 (equivalently, both fields zero-initialized). On crash recovery, N.last_pt and N.last_l are loaded from durable storage (the persisted HLC fence; see §D-X) before resuming operation.'

issues_identified.analysis: The HLC schema defines logical as u16 (16 bits, max 65535). Under high event rate within the same physical_ms (e.g., 100k events/ms inside an in-cell tight loop), the logical counter could overflow. Demirbas+Kulkarni discuss this and recommend either widening the field or stalling until physical_ms advances. The ADR specifies the bit width but not the overflow policy.
issues_identified.recommended_fix: In ADR-0252 §D-1, add: 'Overflow policy: if N.last_l would exceed u16::MAX (65535), the HLC stalls (busy-waits) until monotonic_wall_clock_now_ms advances. This bounds the worst-case stall to 1 ms. In Tier-4 cells with sub-millisecond throughput needs, widen logical to u32 via the v2 schema (forward-declared in /specs/hlc-uncertainty-budget.json).'

issues_identified.issue: Uncertainty budget (±500ms) is stated but not enforced
issues_identified.analysis: ADR-0252 §D-1 says 'uncertainty_budget_ms: u32, cell-configurable; default 500ms' but does not specify what happens when current_uncertainty_ms() exceeds the budget. The algorithm description does not include a divergence-bound check.
issues_identified.recommended_fix: Add: 'When |physical_ms - monotonic_wall_clock_now_ms()| > uncertainty_budget_ms, the HLC emits a SEV-3 alert to ops-sre-reliability and the cell transitions to brown-out per ADR-0176. The HLC continues operating (it does not refuse to issue timestamps) because that would prevent legitimate recovery operations.'

issues_identified.analysis: The pseudocode reads monotonic_wall_clock_now_ms() — but 'monotonic' and 'wall-clock' are different (POSIX CLOCK_MONOTONIC vs CLOCK_REALTIME). True wall-clock can step backward on NTP adjust; monotonic cannot. The HLC algorithm depends on a non-regressing local source. The ADR should clarify it means chronyd-disciplined CLOCK_REALTIME projected through a monotonic max-rule (Demirbas+Kulkarni use 'pt.j' as logical-time, which by construction never regresses).
issues_identified.recommended_fix: Clarify the source: 'monotonic_wall_clock_now_ms = max(N.last_observed_wall_clock, chronyd_disciplined_clock_realtime_ms). This protects against NTP step-back events that would otherwise produce a non-monotonic physical component.'

issues_identified.analysis: ADR-0252 says total HLC = 64-bit physical + 16-bit logical = 80 bits = 10 bytes. The math is correct (64+16=80, 80/8=10). However the ADR also says 'serialised as 12-byte base64' — 10 bytes base64-encoded is 14 chars (with padding) or 14 chars no-pad / 16 chars with-pad. The 12-byte base64 claim doesn't reconcile (12 base64 chars decode to 9 bytes, not 10). This is a minor wire-format documentation defect.
issues_identified.recommended_fix: Either revise the serialised-form description to '14-char base64 no-pad' or '16-char base64 padded' or '20-char hex'. The implementation choice should be specified in /specs/hlc-uncertainty-budget.json.

hlc_algorithm.summary: The HLC algorithm is correctly grounded in Demirbas+Kulkarni 2014. The pseudocode captures the canonical algorithm. Findings are specification-completeness gaps (initial state, overflow, uncertainty enforcement, clock-source semantics, wire-format byte count) rather than algorithmic errors.

tt_truetime_algorithm.notes: TT.now() → TTInterval{earliest, latest}, TT.after(t), TT.before(t) match the canonical Spanner API. Uncertainty bound 7ms default tightened to 1ms when GPS+atomic healthy is consistent with Spanner production reports. Hold-over budgets (Cesium 1µs/day; Rubidium 100µs/day) match Microsemi spec sheets. No defects.

idempotency_key_math.claim: 32-char base32 body = 160 bits entropy = 2^160 ≈ 1.46e48 keys; collision at 2^80
idempotency_key_math.verification: 32 chars × 5 bits/char (base32) = 160 bits. 2^160 ≈ 1.4615e48 — VERIFIED. Birthday bound √(2^160) = 2^80 ≈ 1.21e24 keys before 50% collision; the ADR's '2^80 before 1% collision' is loose but conservative (actual 1%-collision threshold is roughly 2^80 / sqrt(50) ≈ 2^77, which is even smaller, so the claim '2^80 before 1% collision' is actually MORE conservative than reality and is safe).

checks.evidence: ADR-0243 §D-1 defines EvaluationRequest / EvaluationResponse contract; §D-4 composition semantics (permits union; forbids override / deny-wins; NotApplicable). The 'deny wins' tie-break matches AWS Cedar v4 published semantics and AWS Verified Permissions docs. §D-5 bootstrap chain of trust matches PKI root+intermediate canonical pattern (RFC 5280).
findings: Cedar evaluation latency budget <1ms p99 is asserted but not derived from a queuing-theory model; the ADR cites 'AWS Verified Permissions production data' without a quantitative reference. For BLOCKER promotion, suggest adding the per-evaluation operation budget (#policy_evaluations × #attribute_lookups × per-op cost) to /specs/cedar-fragment-schema.json.

checks.evidence: MLS standard correctly cites RFC 9420 §17.1 cipher suite registry, §10 KeyPackage, §7.2 LeafNode, §8 label-prefixed KDF, §9 nonce derivation, §11.6 epoch advancement. Identity model (device-level vs user-level) matches Wickr/Wire production deployments. Safety-number derivation matches Signal canonical.

ADR-0248 §D-7 specifies 'SeededShuffle(seed=tenant_id).permute(pool)[:shard_width]' but does not specify the PRNG or shuffle algorithm. A deterministic shuffle requires a stated PRNG (e.g., ChaCha20-based, SipHash-based, or HMAC-DRBG). Different PRNG choices produce different assignments; future re-implementations could silently diverge.

findings.recommended_fix: In ADR-0248 §D-7, specify the canonical shuffle: 'SeededShuffle = Fisher-Yates shuffle with seed derived as HMAC-SHA-256(canonical_pool_version_id, tenant_id), consuming the seed as a ChaCha20 keystream feeding into a uniform-from-keystream sampler (Lemire 2019 'Fast Random Integer Generation in an Interval').' Add /specs/shuffle-sharding-parameters.json field 'prng_spec' enumerating this choice.

checks.evidence: Standard §3.6 correctly identifies that RFC 9420 does not support in-place cipher-suite migration; the new-group/copy/deprecate pattern is the canonical workaround used by Wire and Wickr.

Standard §3.5.2 says 'concatenate shared secrets, HKDF into final KEM output' but does not specify the HKDF info field (label) used to bind the hybrid context. NIST SP 800-56C and draft-ietf-tls-hybrid-design specify exact concatenation order and label binding to prevent cross-protocol attacks.

findings.recommended_fix: In MLS standard §3.5.2, specify the hybrid KDF as: 'shared_secret = HKDF-Expand-SHA-256(HKDF-Extract-SHA-256(salt=empty, ikm=ss_classical || ss_pq), info="MLS 1.0 hybrid X25519-MLKEM768", L=32)' where ss_classical is X25519 output and ss_pq is ML-KEM-768 output. Cite draft-ietf-mls-pq for the binding label.

checks.evidence: ADR-0252 §D-7 correctly references Google's 24-hour linear smear (chronyd 'slew' mode) and notes the smear applies to wall-clock component only, not logical counter.

ADR-0248 §D-8 prescribes 24-hour cache-validity targets for tenant rows, Cedar fragments, OIDC JWKS, SPIFFE roots, etc. Cache TTL > expected outage window is the correct static-stability rule (Weiss/Furr 2020).
ADR-0248 §D-9 correctly contrasts O(N) snapshot pull vs O(change_rate × fleet_size) push. The Brooker 2020 reference is accurate.
ADR-0243 §D-5 root + intermediate + leaf signing follows RFC 5280 PKI semantics; cosign attestation for fragment immutability matches Sigstore canonical.

MLS standard §3.5.2 implies AES-128-GCM is 'PQ-resistant at 128-bit per Grover's quadratic-speedup mitigation; doubled key size optional.' Grover's algorithm provides O(sqrt(N)) search, effectively halving symmetric key strength against a quantum adversary — i.e., AES-128 falls to ~64-bit quantum security, which is BELOW the typical 128-bit post-quantum security target. NIST SP 800-208 and NSA CNSA 2.0 recommend AES-256 for any post-quantum-resistant deployment requiring 128-bit post-quantum classical-equivalent security.

findings.recommended_fix: Clarify in MLS standard §3.5.2: 'AES-128-GCM provides ~64-bit security against a fully-realized quantum adversary under Grover. For confidentiality lifetimes extending past expected CRQC arrival (2030-2040), upgrade to AES-256-GCM in hybrid suites. AES-128-GCM remains acceptable for short-lived (< 1 year) personal-context messaging where forward secrecy bounds the lifetime, but explicitly NOT acceptable for archived/backup material with multi-year lifetimes.' Adjust §11 (Encrypted backups) accordingly.

checks.evidence: Tier T0/T1/T2/T3 RTO/RPO targets are consistent across ADR-0241 (referenced), ADR-0248, ADR-0252, ADR-0280. SLO floors per substrate (e.g., policy-engine 0.99995; observability 0.999) are coherent with Brooker/Weiss SRE Workbook tier conventions.

ADR-0252 §D-4 fully specifies idempotency key wire format, TTL policy, Postgres schema, request flow with race-condition handling, and ON CONFLICT semantics. Caller-supplied keys + request_signature_hash mismatch detection is the canonical Stripe pattern.
ADR-0252 §D-5 enumerates five narrow exceptions with explicit annotations; matches Kleppmann 'fencing token' acknowledgment and Google SRE Workbook Ch. 24 doctrine.
ADR-0280 §D-3 specifies Tarjan's SCC algorithm for cycle detection; Kahn's algorithm for topological sort. Both are canonical O(V+E) algorithms suitable for the |V|=10 substrate set.

must_fix_before_blocker: A7-F4 (Grover/AES-128 post-quantum caveat) — affects backup material confidentiality lifetime
A7-F5 (hybrid KDF binding label) — affects cross-protocol attack resistance
A7-F7 (shuffle-sharding deterministic PRNG) — affects cross-implementation reproducibility
A7-F8 (HLC initial state + u16 overflow + monotonic semantics) — affects production correctness

alignment_with_oyatie_doctrine.feedback_no_silent_regression: Bundle is consistent — cipher-suite migration, MLS group rekey, idempotency-key TTL, and DAG cycle prevention all forbid silent change.
alignment_with_oyatie_doctrine.feedback_autonomous_implementation_artif: Algorithmic specs are mostly implementation-ready; findings A7-F5, A7-F7, A7-F8 must be closed so that an autonomous implementer cannot diverge from the intent.
alignment_with_oyatie_doctrine.feedback_quality_performance_scalability: Hyperscaler-grade choices are correct (Cedar = AWS Verified Permissions; HLC = CockroachDB; shuffle sharding = AWS Route 53; constant work = AWS Builders' Library; MLS = AWS Wickr, Cisco Webex, Wire).
alignment_with_oyatie_doctrine.feedback_clean_architecture_requirements: Substrate DAG with explicit forbidden_edges_assertion is the cleanest form of inward-only flow at runtime.

sign_off.reviewer_lens_summary: Algorithms are correctly chosen and well-grounded. Defects are specification-completeness (init states, KDF bindings, PRNG choices) and arithmetic-precision (one transcription error, one off-by-2e-4). No algorithm needs replacement; the doctrine is fundamentally sound under the A7 lens.
